findings.reason: the author should extend the owner — declare an `ids` store role in `imas_ambix/data/bundle.py` (or give `_ids_root` the same bundle fallback `_cache` has) — so the writer's `out_root` and the reader's root resolve from one place instead of the script holding the layout the writer's caller set by hand.
findings.text: §3 says "The root is resolved once, in the entry point. It takes `imas_alambic/settings.py` `resolve_settings` (`IMAS_ALAMBIC_IDS_ROOT`) when that yields a root. Otherwise it takes ambix's own development store root, `imas_ambix/data/paths.py` `JT60SA_ROOT / "ids"`", which places the IDS-root layout in the figure script rather than in the owner that resolves store roots by name. The owner is `imas_alambic.machine_map.resolve_store_root` (packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py:303), whose declared roots live in ambix's bundle registrar `imas_ambix/data/bundle.py:19-24` and is already used exactly this way for the sibling `eddb_cache` role by `imas_alambic.settings._cache` (packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/settings.py:162-171); the ids root has its own owner `imas_alambic.settings._ids_root` (settings.py:134-144) but, unlike `_cache`, it has no bundle-role fallback, which is why `resolve_settings` alone yields nothing here. Census of every site that constructs the JT-60SA IDS root: `scripts/figures_jt60sa_signals.py:35` (`pulse_path(Path(JT60SA_ROOT) / "ids", SHOT, RUN)` — the sole such site, and the one §3 would rewrite into the entry-point fallback); `packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/cli.py:87` is the only other reader of the ids root and goes through the owner correctly. No other module constructs it, so §3 would become the first hardcoder of the dev store root outside the owner.

findings.reason: an exact-spec worker cannot implement a function whose boundary is stated two ways; the plan must pin whether the function returns a matplotlib figure (entry point renders) or SVG bytes (function renders), and say which call the entry point makes.
findings.text: §3 says the function "moves the open → `extract_signal_traces` → `time_trace_figure_mpl` → `render_to_bytes` path into one function that takes the run file's root, the pulse, the run number and the series to draw as (IDS name, path) pairs, and returns the figure", then in the next sentence says "It writes nothing; the script's entry point renders each returned figure to SVG and writes it". `render_to_bytes` therefore sits inside the function (which would make it return SVG bytes, not the figure it is stated to return) or in the entry point (which would make it not part of the moved path) — the two statements cannot both hold, and the node's SPEC is exact, so the return type and where the render step lives are undecided.
